name: v1.6.4
body:
## [1.6.4] - 2026-11-20

### Highlights

- **Small questions cost less.** Ask your agent what a function or constant is, or who calls it, and `codegraph_explore` now answers with the definition and every line that uses it, instead of a long answer about related files.
- **Faster answers in Claude Code.** The prompt hook now asks the CodeGraph server already running for your project instead of loading the index again on every prompt, which matters most in large projects, and `codegraph impact` is as fast as it was in 1.6.2 again.
- **Safer on a shared computer.** Each agent session now checks that the background server it connects to runs as you before sending it anything.
- **More of your code in the graph.** Elysia (Bun) routes, PHP includes built from the web server's root or the file's own folder, Dart 3.13 primary constructors and newer Kotlin syntax are now read, and ASP.NET Core routes are named the way ASP.NET serves them.
- **More accurate links.** Dozens of fixes help calls reach the code they mean, most of all in JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, Rust, C#, PHP and Java, and `codegraph affected` no longer picks tests on the far side of an HTTP call, a queue or an event unless you pass `--cross-tier`.
- **Fewer stuck commands.** A `git add` or commit no longer fails with "index.lock: File exists" while CodeGraph syncs, a file whose parse never ends no longer keeps `codegraph init` or sync from finishing, and a server whose project folder was deleted now shuts down.
- **Upgrading:** re-index your projects with `codegraph index` after this release. Many of these fixes are written while indexing, and `codegraph status` and your agent both tell you when an index was built by an older version.

### Security

- On a computer shared with other users, each agent session now checks that the CodeGraph background server it connects to runs as you before sending it anything, and serves the session itself when the server can't prove it, so another user can no longer stand in for your server to read your agent's queries or feed it made-up answers. Thanks @aidenpan0x for pointing it out.

### New Features

- The Claude Code prompt hook now gets its context from the CodeGraph server already running for your project instead of loading the index again on every prompt, so structural prompts are answered sooner, most of all in large projects; with no server running, one that is busy, or one that can't prove it runs as you, the hook works it out itself as before. Thanks @aidenpan0x for the report, the measurements and the pull request. (#3284)
- Elysia (Bun) backends now have their HTTP routes in the graph, named by the full path a request takes, with the prefixes of `new Elysia({ prefix })`, `.group()` and a `.use()` in another file included, and linked to their handlers, so `codegraph_explore` can follow a request from its route into your code. Thanks @ChampPABA for the report. (#3255)
- PHP includes built from the web server's root, like `require $_SERVER['DOCUMENT_ROOT'] . '/inc/header.php'`, now link to their file: CodeGraph works out which folder the server serves from where your includes' paths name files, links nothing when they don't settle it rather than guess, and takes `"webRoot": "public"` in `codegraph.json` (or `"."` for the project root) when you'd rather name it yourself. Thanks @artisanya for the report. (#3298)
- Kotlin is now read with a newer version of its grammar, so code it used to misread, such as an annotated class whose methods showed up as top-level functions, a class that delegates `by` another object, or newer syntax like `when` guards and explicit backing fields, now has its classes, functions and calls in the graph where they belong. (#3410)
- `codegraph_explore` now answers a question about one symbol, like "who calls `toValidURL`?" or "what is `MAX_RETRIES`?", with that symbol's source and every line that uses it, each with the function it sits in and the line's text, instead of filling its whole answer with files that only share words with the name, so these small questions cost less and leave nothing to search for afterwards. Thanks @GeorgeTaveras1231 for the measurements. (#3407)

### Fixes

#### Setup, the background server and the CLI

- `codegraph affected` no longer selects tests on the other side of an HTTP call, a queue or an event, like an Angular app's specs for a change to the Spring controller it calls, since those tests mock that boundary; pass `--cross-tier` to include them. Thanks @jotder for the report. (#3320)
- CodeGraph no longer takes git's index lock while it checks your repository for changes, so a `git add` in a pre-commit hook, a commit or a checkout that runs while CodeGraph syncs no longer fails with "index.lock: File exists". Thanks @iamclaudia-ai for the report. (#3295)
- `codegraph impact` and `codegraph_impact` are as fast as they were in 1.6.2 again, with the same results: 1.6.3 read each symbol's dependents in a way that slowed down every step of the walk. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report and the fix, and @Marcos-199-GitHub for #3285. (#3248)
- When the CodeGraph server's catch-up sync on a large project is stopped because the tool calls it is serving keep its write-ahead log from shrinking, it now waits before trying again, a little longer each time, instead of starting over every second while you keep working. Thanks @kiliman for the report. (#3273)
- A CodeGraph MCP server started in a folder with no index no longer starts its separate hang-watchdog process until the session first calls a tool or opens a project, so sessions that only list the tools, as many hosts open them, use less memory. Thanks @AiurArtanis for the report and @johnhldiver-beep for #3257. (#3250)
- A CodeGraph server whose project folder is deleted, like a removed git worktree, now exits within about half a minute, closing its file watcher and dropping out of the servers `codegraph daemon` lists, instead of running until its last session ends and it times out. On Windows it also stops keeping that folder's index files from being deleted. Thanks @deniskern for the report and @johnhldiver-beep for #3259. (#3245)
- `codegraph upgrade` run from your home folder no longer treats your agents' user-wide setup as a project's: Cursor's CodeGraph server keeps following the workspace you open instead of being pinned to your home folder, and no CodeGraph section is written into `~/AGENTS.md`, `~/GEMINI.md` or `~/QWEN.md`. Thanks @shoma-endo for the report and @b84330808 and @LuisAlbertoMK. (#3234)
- In OpenCode, CodeGraph's instructions, both the ones its server sends and the section `codegraph install` writes to OpenCode's `AGENTS.md`, now name its tools the way OpenCode lists them (`codegraph_codegraph_explore`), so the agent no longer calls a tool name that doesn't exist. Thanks @expiren for the report. (#1267)
- `codegraph init` in a project whose last index run was killed or failed partway now says the index is incomplete and to run `codegraph index`, instead of "Already initialized", which read like a working setup. Thanks @maxmilian for the report and @LuisAlbertoMK. (#3228)
- `codegraph callers`, `callees` and `impact` now warn when a file in the answer changed on disk after it was last indexed, as `codegraph node` and `explore` already did, so a shifted line number no longer reads as a current one. With `--json` the warning goes to stderr and the answer lists those files under `changedOnDisk`. Thanks @arifpambudi242 for the report and @mohitdixit02. (#3260)
- `codegraph status` now reports edits, new files and deletions in gitignored source that `codegraph.json` `include` brings into the index, instead of calling the index up to date until a sync picked them up. Thanks @mixxer for the report and the pull request. (#3086)
- On Linux and macOS, when the system kills CodeGraph with a signal, such as when it runs out of memory during `codegraph init` or `codegraph index`, the command now says which signal and exits as a shell would (137 for SIGKILL), instead of exiting 1 with no message. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report and @johnhldiver-beep. (#3277)
- A Spring or Laravel test's request is now linked only to a route of its own app, not to a JavaScript or TypeScript server's route that happens to match the path, so `codegraph affected` no longer selects Java or PHP tests for a change to your web code. Thanks @jotder for the report. (#3320)

#### Indexing and sync

- `codegraph sync` and the file watcher now follow an edit that adds, removes or repoints a member of an exported object, like `export const api = { getUser, saveUser }`, so a call such as `api.saveUser()` in a file the edit didn't touch links to the new member, or back to the object, as a fresh index does. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3015)
- A file whose parse never ends, like a `.tsx` file with a half-typed JSX attribute, no longer keeps `codegraph init` from exiting or leaves `codegraph sync` and the file watcher spinning at full CPU: its parse now stops at the file's parse time limit, and the file is listed as a parse that timed out. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3274)
- After you upgrade, `codegraph status` and the first CodeGraph answer in each agent session now flag a project indexed by 1.6.3 or earlier as out of date, since this release reads code those indexes are missing, like Dart primary constructors, Elysia routes, PHP includes built from `__DIR__` and the methods of an `export default` object; run `codegraph index` in each project to rebuild it. (#3411)

#### JavaScript and TypeScript

- JavaScript and TypeScript event handlers registered with `on()` are now linked only from code that emits on the same emitter, and to the handler defined where they are registered, so two modules that each keep their own emitter and use the same event name no longer cross-link. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2973)
- In JavaScript, methods written the classic way, `Ctor.prototype.m = function () {…}` and a static `Ctor.m = function () {…}`, are now indexed as methods of their constructor, and the functions of a `module.exports = {…}` object as that module's exports, so `this.m()` inside them reaches the constructor's or the object's own `m` instead of an unrelated function of the same name elsewhere. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2966)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, the functions of an object a module default-exports, like a Vuex store split into `actions.js`, `getters.js` and `mutations.js` (`export default { fetchUser() {…} }`), are now indexed as `default::fetchUser`, so `codegraph_explore`, `node`, `query`, `callers` and impact find them, and a call through the module's default import, `this.fetchUser()` or a Vuex `dispatch('fetchUser')` links to them; a Vuex `commit` now always links to a mutation and a `dispatch` to an action. Thanks @daniel-luan-tran for the report. (#3393)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, `this.findAll()` in a class that wraps an imported helper of the same name now links to the class's own method instead of the imported helper. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2954)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a call written on `this`, like `this.cast()` or `this.validate()`, no longer links to a `const`, a `require` binding or a function declaration that only shares its name, in the same file or another, because what the call reaches is a property of the object.
- In TypeScript, a call on a parameter or local named like an import, like `stream.write()` inside `stream(c, async (stream) => …)`, now goes by that parameter or local, and a method called on an imported function no longer links to the function itself; the same mistake through `require` was already fixed in 1.6.3. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2953)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a call to a name that a function around the caller declares for itself, like a helper an inner arrow function calls, now links to that local declaration instead of the file's import of the same name. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2949)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a call to a helper declared inside a `describe(…)` block, or any other callback, now links to the helper that block declares instead of a same-named one from another block that happens to sit nearer. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2944)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a call inside a spread, like `<input {...register('email')} />` with `register` taken from `useForm()`, no longer links to an unrelated project function that shares the name. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2962)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a module namespace that another module hands on by name, like zod's `import { z } from 'zod'` of `import * as z from './external'; export { z }`, or `export * as ns from './schemas'`, now leads `z.string()` to what that module exports, as `import * as z` does, instead of a same-named method elsewhere. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2951)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, an import through a barrel of several `export *` lines now links to the module that exports the name itself, whichever line comes first, instead of a same-named method of an object another module exports. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3233)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a method called on a variable that a library call fills in, like `const root = createRoot(el)` from react-dom, `net.createServer()` or `canvas.getContext('2d')`, no longer links to the one project method that happens to share its name. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2947)
- In TypeScript, a method called on a variable a class's static factory fills in, like `const writer = DatabaseConnection.initialize(path)`, now links to the method of the class the factory says it returns, instead of a class guessed from the variable's name. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2946)
- In TypeScript, a call through an interface's function-typed property, like `matcher.snapshot()`, no longer links to an unrelated class's method of the same name; a class that implements the interface, or builds it, is still linked. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3035)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a call two or more fields deep from `this`, like `this.cache.list.push(1)` or `this.extractor.functionTypes.includes(type)`, no longer links to an unrelated project method named like JavaScript's own `push`, `includes`, `has` or `set`, or to a property that merely shares the name. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2948)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a `workspaces` entry that points outside the project, like `"../shared"` in `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, no longer makes that folder's package count as part of the project, so a call through an import of it is no longer linked to an unrelated function of yours with the same name. Thanks @bompus for the report and @johnhldiver-beep. (#3093)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a call on a local variable declared after another one in the same statement, like `let n = 0, ob = make()`, or beside a default in a destructuring, like `const { ob = make() } = o`, links again when a variable of the same name outside the function holds a library's type, as it did before 1.6.3. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report and @mohitdixit02. (#3293)
- In JavaScript, a call to a member a required module of your project doesn't have, like `utils.missing()` after `const utils = require('./utils')`, no longer links to an unrelated class's method of that name. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report and @johnhldiver-beep. (#3272)
- A `fetch` or HTTP-client call to another company's API, like `fetch('https://api.github.com/users/…')`, no longer links to your own server's route with the same path; a call to localhost, to a host your code fills in, or through a client's base URL still links. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report and @johnhldiver-beep. (#2974)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a call or `new` of a global, like `parseInt(…)`, `new Response(…)` or `new URL(…)`, in a module that doesn't import that name no longer links to a same-named export of another file in your project. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3238)
- In JavaScript, a `require()` of a folder by a relative path, like `require('..')` from a package's tests, now loads the file the folder's `package.json` names as `main`, as Node does, so calls through it link to the function that file exports. Before, a folder without an `index.js` wasn't followed, and the call linked to the variable holding the `require()` result; on fastify, every test's `Fastify()` linked to its own test file. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2964)
- In JavaScript, a variable that holds what a required module's function returns, like `const app = require('./app')()`, no longer counts as the module itself, so a call like `app.listen()` no longer links to the module's factory function, and links to the method of the class the factory returns when that is known. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#2964)
- In JavaScript and TypeScript, a name imported from a package your `package.json` doesn't list but your project has installed, like `import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form'` hoisted to a monorepo's root `node_modules`, no longer links to an unrelated function of the same name elsewhere in your project (#3271). Re-index JavaScript and TypeScript projects after upgrading.

#### Python

- In Python, `import time` no longer links the importing file to a project function that happens to be named `time`, so such a function stops listing every file that imports the standard library module among its callers and in its impact. The same goes for `json`, `copy`, `random`, `logging` and any other module, and for a fallback variable like `brotli = None` beside a guarded `import brotli`. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3239)
- In Python, a call to a function or method declared with `typing.overload`, like click's `command` and `prompt`, now links to the `def` that runs instead of the first `@overload` stub, so the implementation shows its callers and a call path goes on through it. A stub with no implementation below it, as in a `Protocol`, stays the target, and another library's `overload` whose bodies all run is left alone. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report and @nilotpal-n7. (#2963)
- In Python, a call like `self.create_app()` on an attribute that holds a callable no longer links to a same-named function or variable in another file, nor, when the class sets that attribute itself, to another class's method of that name, so flask's app loading stops showing an example app as its callee. A method the class has, inherits or a subclass overrides still links, as does a function the class stores under that name. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report and @nilotpal-n7. (#2958)
- In Python, a builtin written bare, like `raise TimeoutError(…)`, `class Bad(ValueError)` or `sorted(rows)`, no longer links to a project class or function of that name in a file the code doesn't import, so a project's own `TimeoutError` stops collecting every file that raises the builtin. A name the file defines or imports itself still links. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3232)
- In Python, a call of a name the code around it binds itself, like a local `flat = lambda …`, a parameter, a loop or comprehension variable, a lambda's parameter, or a local or parameter of an enclosing function, no longer links to a module-level function or variable of that name, whether it is in the same file or in one the code never imports. Thanks @inth3shadows for the reports and @johnhldiver-beep. (#3037, #3230, #3231)
- In Python, a local built from a class through its module, like `client = httpx.AsyncClient()`, or bound by `with` or `async with … as client`, now has that class, so `client.get()` links to `AsyncClient.get` instead of the method of a class named like the variable, such as `Client.get`. A `with` whose class hands out something else from `__enter__`, and a class from a module outside your project, still give the local no type. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report and @nilotpal-n7. (#2957)
- In Python, a method called on a local bound from a call, like `made = make(q)` or `s = store.stage()`, now goes by the type the called function or method declares it returns: a `Path`, a `str` or another class from outside your project links nothing, where any project method that happened to share the name could, and one of your own classes links its own method even when other classes have one of that name. Thanks @inth3shadows for the reports and @johnhldiver-beep. (#3038, #3240)
- In Python, a `from x import name` written inside a function now applies to that function only, so calls of `name` in the rest of the file reach the file's own `def name` instead of the imported function, as a wrapper that imports the original it wraps expects. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3229)

#### Java, Kotlin, C# and ASP.NET

- In Java, when two packages declare a class of the same name, a static call, a call on a new object or a call through a variable now reaches the one the calling file can see, including through a wildcard import, and a call written with the package, like `com.x.b.Util.log(…)`, reaches that package's class. Thanks @inth3shadows for the reports and @johnhldiver-beep. (#2976, #3290, #3291)
- In Kotlin, an extension declared on an import alias of a library type, like `fun DeclAlias.pad()` after `import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier as DeclAlias`, now links from calls on that type, whatever name the calling file imports it under. Thanks @mixxer for the report and the pull request. (#3084)
- In C#, a method called on what a method of the same class returns, like `GetMailer().Send()`, now links to the method of the type that method is declared to return. Thanks @Gobakabana for the report. (#2906)
- In ASP.NET Core, attribute routes are now named the way ASP.NET serves them: `[controller]` and `[action]` are filled in, each controller uses its own `[Route]` (or its base controller's), `~/` paths stand alone, and actions marked `[HttpHead]`, `[HttpOptions]` or `[AcceptVerbs]`, with their own `[Route]`, or in an attribute list are no longer missed. Thanks @Gobakabana for the report. (#2905)
- In C#, an extension method is now matched by the type its `this` parameter takes, so `"hi".Shout()` and `mailer.Shout()` each reach their own extension, and a call of a string's own method no longer reaches a project extension of the same name. Thanks @Gobakabana for the report. (#2906)
- In C#, a method called through `?.` or `!.`, like `_mailer?.Send()`, now links to the method of the receiver's type. Thanks @Gobakabana for the report. (#2906)
- In C#, a method passed or stored as a value through its object, like `Task.Run(worker.Run)` or `Action later = worker.Run;`, now counts as a use of that method, so `codegraph callers` and impact show it. Thanks @Gobakabana for the report. (#2906)
- In Kotlin, a call named after a modifier keyword at the start of a statement, like `annotation("jakarta.persistence.Entity")` in a Gradle `allOpen { }` block or a class's own `open()`, is now read as the call it is, so a build script made of such calls no longer warns that it contributes nothing to the graph. Thanks @clayly for the report. (#3410)

#### PHP and Laravel

- In PHP, a method called on a freshly built object, like `(new SettingClient())->getSet(1)`, now links to the class the file's namespace and `use` imports name, or to a method it inherits, so these calls show up in `callers` and impact. Thanks @holysor for the report. (#3244)
- In Laravel, a route written like `[UserController::class, 'show']` now links to the controller the routes file imports, through a plain or aliased `use`, a group `use`, an imported namespace or a fully qualified name, instead of a same-named controller elsewhere or nothing. Thanks @inth3shadows for the reports and @johnhldiver-beep. (#2975, #3292)
- In PHP, a method called in a different letter case than its declaration, like `PriceConverter::CalcBasePrice(1)` or `$c->GetRate()` for `calcBasePrice` and `getRate`, now links to that method, as PHP reads method names without regard to case, so those calls show up in `callers` and impact. Thanks @artisanya for the report and @johnhldiver-beep. (#3297)
- In PHP code written for PHP 7 and older, a string offset in braces, like `$code{0}`, no longer makes the function or class around it disappear from the index with its calls credited to the file; it now reads like `$code[0]`. Thanks @artisanya for the report. (#3299)
- In PHP, a `require` or `include` of a file inside a function or method now counts as that function depending on the file, so `callers` and impact follow code in the included file back to the function and its callers. Thanks @artisanya for the report. (#3296)
- In PHP, an include built from the file's own directory, like `require_once __DIR__ . '/inc/a.php'` or `dirname(__FILE__) . '/inc/b.php'`, now links to that file the way a plain `require_once 'lib.php'` does, and a path starting with `./` or `../` links only to the file named exactly, as PHP loads it, never one with `.php` added. Thanks @artisanya for the report and @inth3shadows. (#3298)

#### Rust

- In Rust, a call through a module that a glob `use` brings in, like `gzip::write()` in a test module with `use super::*`, or that a `use` inside the function names, now links to that module's function again. Thanks @Egrn for the report and @mohitdixit02. (#3253)
- In Rust, `codegraph_explore`'s blast radius now recognizes unit tests in a `#[cfg(test)]` module or a `tests.rs` file, instead of reporting "no tests found" for the functions they test. Thanks @moogiemode for the report and @maxmilian. (#3265)
- In Rust, a function or method passed as a value through its path, like `g.map(Graph::counts)` or `.map(Self::helper)`, now counts in its callers and impact the way a function passed by name already did, linked only when the path names it for certain: never another type's method of the same name, and never a method of a trait implementation, since which one Rust uses there depends on the type of the argument. Thanks @Egrn for the report and @inth3shadows. (#3254)
- In Rust, a call on a value whose type comes from outside your project, like an outside crate's builder chain or `stdout.flush()`, no longer links to one of your methods that only shares its name, such as your own `impl Write`'s `write` and `flush` or an associated function like `Graph::build(n)`, and `Rules::default()` on a `#[derive(Default)]` type no longer links to another type's `default`. Thanks @Egrn for the report. (#3252)
- In Rust, a call written in the arguments of `format!`, `println!`, `write!`, `assert_eq!`, `vec!`, `matches!` or serde_json's `json!` now links to the function or method it calls, as the same call outside the macro does, and a variant in a `matches!` pattern now counts as a use of its enum. Thanks @Egrn for the report. (#3251)

#### Go, Swift, Dart, C and C++

- A C++ `.h` header that only declares functions and `extern` variables, with no class, namespace or template in it, is now read as C++ when it uses a template type like `CComPtr<IDiaDataSource>`, a reference parameter like `bstr_t& path` or `const qstring &name`, or a default argument like `int depth = 0`, instead of as C, which dropped its symbols and warned "parse produced no symbols (tree has errors)". Thanks @sonyps5201314 for the report. (#3397)
- In Swift, a type no longer picks up the inheritance of a type nested inside it, which linked a name used in the type to an unrelated type's nested type and put it in the wrong impact results. Thanks @bob-codedaptive for the report and @remote-controlled-man. (#3213)
- In Go, a method called on `new(T)` or `make(T)` now links to that type's method, not a same-named method of another type that happened to be found first. Thanks @inth3shadows for the report. (#3237)
- In Swift, an `if` or `while` whose condition is `try await f()` no longer breaks the method around it: the next member landed inside that method, and calls were recorded under names made of source text. Swift files are now read with a newer Swift grammar, which also parses more Swift 6 code without errors. Thanks @bob-codedaptive for the report. (#3212)
- In Dart, a class declared with a Dart 3.13 primary constructor, like `class Point(final int x, final int y) {…}` or `class const Foo({required final int a})`, is now indexed under its own name with its members, where it had been named `const` or dropped with the rest of its file; Dart files are now read with a newer Dart grammar, which also parses dot shorthands and other recent Dart syntax without errors. Thanks @cutehackers for the report. (#3270)

name: v1.4.0-rc.4
body:
## beads v1.4.0-rc.4

Pre-compiled binaries for Linux, macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon), Windows (AMD64 & ARM64), Android/Termux (ARM64), and FreeBSD.

### Installation (release candidate)

> **This is a prerelease for validation.** The stable install channels —
> Homebrew, the `install.sh` / `install.ps1` scripts, npm, and PyPI —
> intentionally keep serving the latest **stable** release, so they will **not**
> install this RC. Use one of the methods below.

**Manual download (recommended):**
Download the archive for your platform from the **Assets** below, extract it,
and place `bd` on your PATH.

**Go install (pinned to this RC):**
```bash
go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@v1.4.0-rc.4
# For embedded Dolt support:
CGO_ENABLED=1 GOFLAGS=-tags=gms_pure_go go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@v1.4.0-rc.4
```

> **1.4.0 is a one-way upgrade. Back up first, with your current bd.** Consenting to the schema migration (`bd migrate schema`, `--force`, or `BD_ALLOW_MIGRATE=1`) moves a 1.2.x or 1.3.x store to schema v74. After that, bd 1.3.x and older refuse the database; going back means restoring a backup. From 1.4.0-rc.1, rc.2 or rc.3, rc.4 is a binary swap: it adds no migration.
>
> - Validate on a copy, or on a store you have backed up with your current bd (`bd dolt push`, a JSONL export, or `bd backup sync`).
> - Every Dolt server bd talks to, and the `dolt` CLI on `PATH`, must be 2.6.0 or newer.
> - Read **Upgrade notes** and **Known issues** under `[1.4.0-rc.4]`, `[1.4.0-rc.3]`, `[1.4.0-rc.2]` and `[1.4.0-rc.1]` in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.4.0-rc.4/CHANGELOG.md) before installing.
>
> **New in rc.4:**
> - Go programs that link beads can open a proxied-server workspace with `beads.OpenBestAvailable` ([#8323](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/8323)). It used to return no error and open a new, empty embedded store at `.beads/embeddeddolt` there (cgo builds). It now goes through the workspace's bd proxy: it adopts a running proxy or starts one from the `bd` on `PATH`; with no `bd` there, or with a proxy that a bd older than 1.4 started (left running), it fails with `beads.ErrProxyUnavailable`. A managed-local workspace also needs `dolt` on `PATH` (or `BEADS_DOLT_BIN`), even to adopt a running proxy. Forcing server mode and naming a plain Dolt server's port in `BEADS_DOLT_SERVER_PORT` keeps the direct server connection (a 1.4 proxy's data port accepts only bd). The returned store does not serve every `Storage` method; see `[1.4.0-rc.4]` for its differences from `DoltStore`. `beads.Open`, `OpenFromConfig` and `OpenGated` are unchanged (see **Still open**).
> - On a proxied-server workspace whose database has a Dolt remote (`bd init --proxied-server` adds one from git `origin` by default), the remote-migrate refusal no longer offers `bd migrate --force`, `BD_ALLOW_REMOTE_MIGRATE=1 bd migrate`, `bd dolt push`, `bd dolt pull` or `bd bootstrap`, which are refused there or create a separate local database. It names `bd migrate schema --force`, run on one clone of that remote only with the proxy's library clients stopped ([#8568](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/8568)). Server and embedded mode are unchanged.
> - On a shared or external Dolt server and in proxied-server workspaces, the refusals a 1.3.x upgrade meets, and the `bd upgraded to …: N schema migration(s) pending` notice, no longer say read commands keep working until you migrate: every issue read needs `arrival_seq` (migration 0073), so until `bd migrate schema` runs an upgraded client can neither read nor write issues. Upgrade every client and migrate in one sitting ([#8571](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/8571)).
>
> **From rc.3:**
> - Telemetry no longer exports issue content. Correction to the rc.1 notes: with the console trace exporter on (`BD_OTEL_ENABLED=true` with `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=console`, or the legacy `BD_OTEL_STDOUT=true` on its own), rc.1 and rc.2 still wrote titles, descriptions, notes, labels, comments and search text to stderr in the `bd.args` span attribute ([#8505](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/8505)); logs that kept bd's stderr can hold it. `bd.args` now names only the command and the flags that were set, so trace queries that read its values must change.
> - bd ranks a release candidate below its release ([#6595](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6595)). Moving from a candidate to 1.4.0 records the release in the version marker in proxied-server workspaces and on a Dolt server whose data is in `.beads/dolt`; in shared-server mode and on other external servers `bd doctor` keeps reporting the candidate until you run bare `bd migrate` once per database.
>
> **Behavior changes to know before installing** (from rc.2):
> - `bd github` now stops when a repository lookup fails. Rerun after a temporary failure. Never clear or repoint another repository's bead links to get past it: the next sync creates unlinked beads as new issues in the configured repository.
> - Server-mode pulls need EXECUTE on `dolt_fetch` and `dolt_merge`.
> - `bd backup restore` refuses a Dolt server on another host. Run it on the server's machine, in a workspace that names the same `dolt_database`.
>
> **Still open:**
> - [#7283](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/7283): after `bd migrate schema` the recorded bd version can stay at 1.3.x in every mode; in server mode `bd doctor` reports it — run bare `bd migrate` once per database (embedded too; proxied-server mode refuses it and nothing there acts on the marker). See the corrections under `[1.4.0-rc.4]` **Known issues**.
> - From 1.3.x, `bd ready` prints no upgrade notice and `bd upgrade status` says `upgraded: false`: read these notes, or run `bd info --whats-new` after `bd migrate schema` (bd refuses it before).
> - Go programs that open a proxied-server workspace with `beads.Open`, `OpenFromConfig` or `OpenGated` still go around its proxy: `Open` can create an empty database, and with no proxy running the other two start a Dolt server that blocks bd until it is killed. Use `OpenBestAvailable` ([#8412](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/8412), [#8323](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/8323)).
> - On a proxied-server workspace, no bd command adopts a remote that another clone has already migrated, and the adopt and fork stops still name `bd bootstrap` (which creates a separate local database there). bd can't refresh its copy of the remote in that mode, so check with the other clones before you migrate one. See **Known issues** under `[1.4.0-rc.4]` for the manual adopt route.
> - Only bd can use a proxied-server workspace's proxy data port (since rc.1). A plain MySQL client, or a gc release that reads a proxied rig directly, is closed after 5 seconds with nothing sent (`ERROR 2013 (HY000): Lost connection to server at 'handshake: reading initial communication packet'`), and `proxy.log` records it only if the proxy was started with `BD_DEBUG=1`. Run SQL with `bd sql`.
> - `bd create --repo <url>`'s cached clone still writes the URL into merge commits ([#8434](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/8434)).
>
> When 1.4.0 ships, install it by hand. Server-mode `bd doctor` on rc.3 or rc.4, run in a terminal, also tells you; nothing tells you on rc.1 or rc.2, on an embedded or proxied-server workspace, or when `bd doctor` runs under an agent, a script or `--json`.


## Changelog
### Features
* ef08cbaf659466ea4e2cd3ee5f623d32826d377e feat(sdk): route proxied-server workspaces through the bd proxy (GH#8323) (#8558) (#8563)
### Bug Fixes
* 89b5bfe0e7af3536d694c3ff960f9b1708864dd5 fix(migrate): give proxied-server workspaces a remote-migrate refusal they can act on (bd-5hl9dg) (#8568)
* b97fce2a56336e94e76fe37d927d93e4a789c843 fix(migrate): stop promising that reads keep working before a schema migration (#8571)
* 7c0e969e269d08e19781f4af87c6a52a78615622 fix(uow): restore #8571's readOnly comment hunk dropped in the backport resolution
### Others
* 5cd368a4ba624cc3c99fe415cf7515d3fbc7b734 chore(release): fold #8568 into v1.4.0-rc.4 notes; date rc.4 2026-11-20
* cdd563ce00235a34dc8f252407ce900c1dde9dc2 chore(release): fold #8571 into v1.4.0-rc.4 notes; correct earlier rc notes from the upgrade drill
* cde822f3895c84e546fdbe4312f14ce2ea7ba97d chore(release): prepare v1.4.0-rc.4
* f7e572f8495839a41e1d34628e21bcbdbc339490 docs(release): correct rc.4 adopt known issue and --force guidance (#8569 review)

name: v0.22.12
body:
# oh-my-codex v0.22.12

## Summary

This patch release ships a fix for recovering quarantined live-pin lock links from JSONL record streams in team state. The fix improves reliability of team lock recovery when processing stored JSONL records.

## Fixed

- **RECOVER QUARANTINED LIVE-PIN LOCK LINKS (#4112):** Fixed deserialization of live-pin tracking data from JSONL streams. Quarantined lock links in team state were not being properly recovered due to incomplete deserialization logic. Lock recovery now correctly processes all stored JSONL records. Fixes #4111.

## Compatibility

No breaking API changes. Release-coupled metadata (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, Cargo workspace, and plugin metadata) all report `0.22.12`.

## Verification

- Full CI on dev candidate (candidate details recorded in [release readiness](docs/qa/release-readiness-0.22.12.md)).
- PR #4112 CI passed on merged head.

## Contributors

Thanks to [@iqdoctor](https://github.com/iqdoctor), Watch, and [@Yeachan-Heo](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo) for contributing to this release.

**Full Changelog**: [`v0.22.11...v0.22.12`](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex/compare/v0.22.11...v0.22.12)

—
*[repo owner's gaebal-gajae (clawdbot) 🦞]*

name: CC Switch v4.0.38
body:
# CC Switch v4.0.38

本版本以修复为主。一键导入链接现在可以导入 **WorkBuddy** 供应商；Linux 上也能在授权中心切换 **Antigravity** 账号；Antigravity 的会话列表不再混进空会话和内部子会话，会话阅读器能看到思考、工具调用和结果。

另外修复了 DeepSeek Harness 的配置文件经过某些 YAML 工具后，所有第三方供应商都消失；从访达打开 CC Switch 时，「应用」页把能正常用的 npm 安装标成「无法运行」；技能仓库不是 GitHub / GitLab / Gitea 时只提示「0 个技能」而不报错；Codex 给模型选的思考等级有时没生效；Codex 经路由的几处格式转换错误；用量重复计算；会话正文搜索失败时显示「没有会话包含这个词」；主界面变成一条白条或被 macOS 菜单栏遮住；Linux AppImage 里点链接没反应等问题。

**[English →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.38-en.md) | [日本語版 →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.38-ja.md)**

---

## 新增

### WorkBuddy 支持一键导入链接

`ccswitch://` 供应商链接现在可以导入 WorkBuddy 供应商（[#9768](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9768)），生成的卡片和在 WorkBuddy 页手动添加的一样。

- 链接必须带模型；`apiFormat` 只支持 `openai_chat`。
- 模型 ID 已被别的卡片占用时，导入会被拒绝，不会留下半截卡片。

### Linux 上切换 Antigravity 账号

Linux 上也能在授权中心管理 agy 的登录、切换账号，官方卡片上显示所绑定账号的额度（[#9774](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9774)，相关 [#9245](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9245)）。

- 登录凭据存在系统的钥匙串（Secret Service）里。钥匙串锁着时，后台查状态和额度会跳过，主动切号时会请求解锁。
- Linux 上绑了账号的卡片，「打开终端」对话框里多了「本次使用 agy 当前登录」：本机没有绑定的账号或钥匙串不可用时，可以先用当前登录打开终端，卡片的绑定保留不变。

---

## 变更

- **Antigravity 会话列表和会话阅读器**（[#9266](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9266)，见 [#9265](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9265)）：在终端里只查一下 `/usage` 就退出留下的空会话（显示为 `Jan 1`）、已删除或从别的设备同步来的残留记录、`/boost` 子代理和 `/btw` 旁路提问不再出现在列表里，它们的用量照常统计。没有标题的会话用预览或第一句提问当标题。会话阅读器能看到思考、正文、工具调用（含 MCP、浏览器等）和工具结果（含命令退出码、中断状态），文件改动显示增删行数。升级后会话正文索引会自动重建一次。
- **会话搜索和用量统计更快**（[#9823](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9823)、[#9825](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9825)）：会话页切换应用时不再为每个会话 ID 和路径重建搜索索引，内存占用也小得多；用量统计的查询能用上数据库索引，首字时间只读一遍，价格每次查询只加载一次。
- **授权中心里 Google 账号的套餐名去掉多余的「Google」**（[#9834](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9834)）：Antigravity 和 Gemini CLI 账号的「Google AI Pro」现在显示为「AI Pro」。

---

## 修复

- **DeepSeek Harness 里所有第三方供应商突然消失**（见 [#9785](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9785)）：`cordis.patch.yml` 经过某些 YAML 工具保存后，思考档位里的 `off` 会变成 `false`。CC Switch 以前会原样存下来、每次同步都写回去，DeepSeek Harness 因为这一个非法键把整段供应商配置都判为无效。现在读写时都会改正（`false` 改回 `off`，不认识的档位去掉）。
- **从访达打开 CC Switch 时，「应用」页把能正常用的 npm 安装标成「无法运行」**（见 [#9810](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9810)）：检测安装时用的 PATH 里找不到 node，用 `npm --prefix`、volta、pnpm、bun 等方式装的命令行工具就会被判成无法运行，界面还会建议重装或卸载。现在检测时带上登录 shell 的 PATH，和 CC Switch 运行其他命令行工具时一样。Windows 不受影响。
- **添加不支持的站点（如 cnb.cool）上的技能仓库时，只提示「0 个技能」而不报错**（见 [#9812](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9812)）：这类站点对任何地址都返回一个网页，以前下载到的网页被当成压缩包，失败了也没有提示。现在会提示「下载到的不是压缩包：这个站点可能不是 GitHub / GitLab / Gitea 仓库，暂不支持」。
- **Codex 给模型手动选的思考等级（如 `max`、`ultra`）有时没生效**（[#9017](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9017)，见 [#8952](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8952)）：模型名和 Codex 官方模型对得上时，生成的模型目录用的是官方的思考等级。现在按卡片里选的写入。
- **Codex 经路由转成 Chat 格式时，名字相近的工具会撞名**（[#9554](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9554)，见 [#9551](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9551)）：工具名或命名空间里自带 `__` 时，以前可能丢掉工具，或者把调用发给错的工具。现在每个工具都有唯一的名字，调用能准确对回去。
- **Codex 经路由用过第三方模型的对话，切到官方模型后无法继续**（[#9756](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9756)，见 [#9054](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9054)）：转换出来的消息 ID 以 `resp_` 开头，官方接口要求以 `msg_` 开头，直连模式下会报 `invalid_id_prefix`。新生成的 ID 改为 `msg_` 开头；已经存下的旧对话不变。
- **Codex 经路由连 AWS Bedrock 上的 Claude 时，每个请求都报 400**（[#8659](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8659)，见 [#6118](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/6118)）：工具定义里多带了 OpenAI 专用的 `strict` 字段，Bedrock 不接受。现在不再转发这个字段。
- **用量重复计算**：
  - 模型名带网关前缀（如 `antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash-high`）时，同一个请求在路由记录和 Codex 会话日志里各算一次（[#9249](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9249)）。现在去掉前缀再比对。
  - Gemini 旧会话文件更新后，已经归档的用量又被导入一次；会话里的 token 数变了却没有更新（[#9527](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9527)，见 [#9523](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9523)）。
- **用量统计里 Codex 的缓存写入显示 N/A**（[#8191](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8191)）：现在显示实际数值，只有 Gemini 和 Grok Build 仍显示 N/A（它们不上报缓存写入）。请求日志也不再把 Codex 的缓存写入算进新输入。
- **Antigravity 的输出速度显示为估算值，偏低**（[#9788](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9788)，见 [#9787](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9787)）：Antigravity 自己记录了首字时间和流式输出时长，以前没用上，速度按总耗时（含首字前的等待）估算。现在和经路由的请求一样按实际输出时长计算。
- **会话正文搜索出错时，显示「没有会话包含这个词」**（[#9512](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9512)，见 [#9511](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9511)）：现在会提示「正文搜索失败，暂时只能按标题、目录和首末消息查找」，可以点「重试」，重试时会把会话重新收录进索引。
- **OpenCode 会话的两个边界问题**（[#7982](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/7982)）：迁移到新格式后又在 OpenCode 1.x 里继续的会话，以前显示的是旧内容；新格式迁移中途中断时，没迁完的会话不再被隐藏。
- **Oh My Pi 的恢复会话命令在 Windows 上粘贴到 PowerShell 会报错**（[#9153](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9153)，见 [#9152](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9152)）：Windows 上现在生成 PowerShell 写法，macOS 和 Linux 不变。
- **Linux AppImage 里点链接在浏览器中打开、或打开文件夹，没有任何反应**（[#9113](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9113)，见 [#9112](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9112)）：AppImage 自带的旧版 xdg-open 在 KDE Plasma 6 下什么都不做。现在改用系统自己的 xdg-open。deb / rpm、macOS 和 Windows 不受影响。
- **macOS 上把全屏的主界面关到托盘，再打开时被菜单栏和 Dock 遮住**（[#9770](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9770)，见 [#9769](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9769)）：现在关到托盘前先退出全屏，从托盘、Dock 等再打开时恢复全屏。
- **主界面打开后只是一条白条**（[#9504](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9504)，见 [#9496](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9496)）：记住的窗口尺寸异常小时，打开时恢复成默认大小。
- **编辑供应商时，关掉还在保存的编辑器再打开，「保存」按钮一直转圈**（[#9593](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9593)，见 [#9592](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9592)）。
- **Copilot 旧版登录迁移遇到网络超时就放弃，要重启才会再试**（[#9549](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9549)，见 [#9544](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9544)）：现在网络恢复后，下次用到 Copilot 时会继续迁移，不用重启；只有令牌失效（401 / 403）或退出登录才放弃。
- **中转站地址被误认成官方厂商**（[#9648](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9648)）：地址的路径或参数里出现官方域名，或者域名长得像（如 `api.x.ai.example.com`）时，以前会被当成那家厂商：xAI 走专门的处理，余额和套餐额度也按那家的官方模板查。现在只看真正的域名。
- **导入配置、云同步下载等操作中，累加式应用有供应商没写进配置文件，却提示成功**（[#9747](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9747)）：现在会列出写入失败的供应商。
- **移动技能存储位置后，有应用没能重新链接，却提示成功**（[#9748](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9748)）：现在会在提示里列出来。

---

## 致谢

感谢 @thisTom（WorkBuddy 一键导入链接）、@Railgun-wiki（Linux 上切换 Antigravity 账号、Antigravity 会话）、@jimpablo（Antigravity 会话）、@YUZHEthefool（会话搜索和用量统计提速）、@StrengW（Codex 思考等级）、@HaiYangBG1（Codex 工具撞名、Copilot 登录迁移、Gemini 用量重复计算）、@Logic-Bin（Codex 消息 ID）、@zihenghe04（Bedrock 的 `strict` 字段）、@AkimioJR（网关前缀用量去重）、@Chaoqi31（Codex 缓存写入）、@lyfuci（Antigravity 输出速度）、@jzcangshu（会话正文搜索失败提示）、@ISuuuu（OpenCode 会话）、@wlndysky（Oh My Pi 恢复命令）、@NeoChen1024（AppImage 打开链接）、@fuyundev（macOS 全屏窗口）、@1clipse（主界面白条）、@MonsterXia（编辑器保存转圈）、@SaladDay（中转地址误认、失败提示、代码整理）、@funkpopo、@allenxu09（评审修改）的贡献。

特别感谢 @kense-lab：你的 PR 发现并修复了 Codex 经路由连 Bedrock 时 `strict` 字段被拒的问题，只是同样的问题后来用另一种改法修好，PR 因此关闭。

感谢 @zhmmartin、@308521201-stack（同时给出了修法）、@Gitzzr、@Duosl、@LyciumRuthenicum、@AlanQi1 报告问题和提供复现信息。

完整的技术细节请见 [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)。

name: CC Switch v4.0.37
body:
# CC Switch v4.0.37

本版本以修复为主。读不出来的供应商和 MCP 条目（比如由更新版本写入、经 WebDAV / S3 同步过来的）不再被当成空配置、下次保存时被默认值覆盖，而是单独列出来，可以删除；Pi 新增 **Mistral AI** 预设；韩语界面翻译整体改进。

另外修复了本地路由监听地址填 IPv6 时启动不了；「应用到 Claude Code 插件」会把损坏的 `~/.claude/config.json` 整个清空；网速慢时大的技能仓库下载到一半被中断；从访达打开 CC Switch 时 Codex 模型目录探测找不到 Node；工具调用参数里 `_` 开头的字段被删掉后才发给上游；移出又加回故障转移队列的供应商仍被跳过；插件页点「重试」看起来没反应等问题。

**[English →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.37-en.md) | [日本語版 →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.37-ja.md)**

---

## 新增

### Pi 新增 Mistral AI 预设

Pi 新增 Mistral AI 预设，走 Pi 自己的 Mistral 协议（`mistral-conversations`），流式的思考内容不会丢（需求见 [#9343](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9343)，[#9344](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9344)）。

- 自带 Mistral Large 4 和 Mistral Small 4，思考档位与 Pi 内置的 Mistral 目录一致。
- 供应商名为 `cc-switch-mistral`，不会遮住 Pi 内置的 `mistral`。
- Pi 表单的协议列表里也可以选 `mistral-conversations`。Oh My Pi 和 Kimi Code 不支持这个协议，不显示这个预设。

---

## 变更

- **读不出来的供应商和 MCP 条目原样保留，可以单独删除**（[#9767](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9767)）：以前数据读不出来时会被当成空配置，下次保存就把默认值写回去，原来的数据丢了。现在这样的条目在供应商页和 MCP 页单独列出，显示读不出来的原因，不能编辑或启用，可以删除（只删 CC Switch 里的记录，不动各应用的配置文件）；其他条目照常显示和使用，故障转移跳过它；改这一条的操作会被拒绝，有这样的条目时，累加式应用（如 OpenCode）把全部供应商同步到配置文件也会报错。升级到能读的版本后即可恢复。
- **Claude Code 的 1M 标记改写成小写 `[1m]`**（见 [#9757](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9757)）：和 Claude Code 文档写法一致。Claude Code 本来不区分大小写，已有的 `[1M]` 照常可用。
- **韩语界面翻译改进**（[#9395](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9395)，[#9349](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9349)）。
- **授权中心的账号行更好读**（[#9369](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9369)）：「N 个供应商在用」单独一行，额度名称列按最长的名称定宽，窗口窄时套餐、域名和登录日期不再被挤成省略号；德语、俄语等较长的翻译也能看到百分比。

---

## 修复

- **本地路由的监听地址填 IPv6（如 `::1`）时启动不了**（见 [#9743](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9743)）：以前会报「invalid socket address syntax」，现在可以正常监听。
- **开了「应用到 Claude Code 插件」后，损坏的 `~/.claude/config.json` 会被清空**（见 [#9744](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9744)）：文件不是合法 JSON 时，以前当成空文件重写，里面的其他设置都丢了。现在会报错并指出文件路径，文件原样不动；写入也改成先写临时文件再替换，中途中断不会留下半截文件。
- **网速慢时，大的技能仓库下载到一半被中断**：安装、更新、检查更新和发现技能以前都限制整个下载 60 秒。现在只有连续 60 秒收不到数据才中止，并提示「没有收到数据」；整个下载最长 10 分钟。
- **从访达打开 CC Switch 时，Codex 模型目录探测找不到 Node**（见 [#9764](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9764)）：用 npm 装的 Codex 因此运行失败，CC Switch 退回用 Codex 桌面版自带、可能较旧的 CLI，聚合模式下的 GPT 模型少了官方信息（比如搜索工具）。现在探测时带上登录 shell 的 PATH，和 CC Switch 运行其他命令行工具时一样。
- **工具调用参数里 `_` 开头的字段被删掉后才发给上游**（[#9753](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9753)）：MCP、数据库、GraphQL 类工具常用 `_id`、`_meta`、`__typename` 这类字段，以前会被当成私有字段删掉，模型看到的调用和实际执行的不一样，严格的供应商可能直接拒绝请求。现在工具调用参数原样保留。
- **从故障转移队列移出再加回的供应商，卡片显示正常但仍会被跳过一段时间**（[#9750](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9750)）：移出队列或退出某个应用的路由时，现在会同时清掉运行中的熔断状态。开启 OMO / OMO Slim 时没能删掉另一个变体的配置文件，现在也会单独提示。
- **插件页加载超时后点「重试」看起来没反应**（见 [#9758](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/9758)）：已安装、发现和市场三个页签在重试时都会显示加载中。
- **插件页的几处问题**（[#9742](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9742)）：切到别的应用再切回来，进行中的操作仍显示转圈；Codex 更新插件期间又把它启用，更新结束后不会再被停用；搜索也能按显示名搜到（Pi 通过 git 或本地目录安装的包）；卸掉固定版本的 Pi 包、再从「发现」安装后，它不再留在「发现」里；Windows 上装在 WSL 里的插件现在能显示版本、名称和描述。
- **内存和资源占用**（[#9773](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9773)）：离开会话阅读器时释放缓存的图片；关闭自动更新时释放已下载的安装包；部分网络请求复用 HTTP 连接，不再每次新建；本地路由收到的请求体（含解压后）上限为 200 MiB，超过返回 413。
- **安装或升级命令行工具后，紧接着的操作偶尔提示「正在进行中」**（[#9775](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/9775)）。

---

## 致谢

感谢 @SaladDay（读不出来的条目原样保留、熔断状态清理、工具锁释放顺序、清理无用代码）、@vastStage（工具调用参数保留 `_` 字段）、@funkpopo（插件页修复、授权中心账号行）、@alterxyz（Pi 的 Mistral AI 预设）、@Owlbay（内存和资源占用）、@allenxu09（授权中心账号行）、@cuiyf5516（韩语翻译）的贡献。

感谢 @vastStage、@xxy9468615、@tanghululalala、@JohnZhong505 报告问题和提供复现信息。

完整的技术细节请见 [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)。

name: v4.1.27
body:
### Added

- LM Studio settings have an API key field, for servers with "Require Authentication" turned on.
- The MCP tab shows a "read-only" badge on tools whose server declares them read-only.
- The Account view has a Privacy settings link to the Cline web app's data-use preferences.
- The extension package now includes its third-party license notices.

### Changed

- With no saved model, the Cline provider now starts on the first free model instead of Claude Sonnet 5.5. Saved selections are untouched.
- The reasoning effort dropdown shows the effort a new task will actually use, and has a Default entry that clears the saved setting.
- A provider's model list refreshes after you save its API key or base URL, and a failed refresh (such as a rejected key) shows as an error in the model picker.
- `read_files` results are no longer cut to 8k characters on the way to the model. A read now arrives in full, up to the tool's own limit of 2000 lines or about 48k characters.
- Refreshed the model catalog. Adds 94 providers from models.dev and drops Lilac and Tempr. The Cline recommended list adds Muse Ember. The Cline free list drops Reflection Beam, Laguna S 2.1 and Solar Mini 4. ClinePass drops DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Mimo V2.6 Flash, Mimo V2.6 Pro, MiniMax M3, Qwen3.7 Plus and Qwen3.7 Max. Default models change for 67 other providers, mostly to Kimi K3.1 Pro, Gemini 4 Neon (including the `gemini` and `vertex` providers) or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017.

### Fixed

- Picking "None" for reasoning effort is now saved and sent. Before, GPT-6 on Azure kept its default effort and rejected tool calls.
- Turning reasoning off now reaches custom models that have saved Model Configuration overrides. Before, gpt-5.6 and gpt-6 chat-completions endpoints rejected every tool call.
- On the native OpenAI provider, the reasoning level is fitted to what each model supports, so `max` and Extra High are no longer rejected by GPT-5.x and o-series models.
- Reflection Beam no longer fails every turn with `400 Missing required parameter: 'messages[n].reasoning_content'` after a compaction or a model switch.
- Compaction no longer falls back to the basic summary on models the catalog doesn't describe.
- LiteLLM: the legacy `max_tokens` field is no longer used as the input budget when the model reports `max_output_tokens`.
- Reasoning text from a turn that was cancelled or failed no longer shows up at the start of the next turn's reasoning.
- Commit search passes your query to git as arguments instead of shell text, so a quoted search matches the exact phrase.
- Security: undici raised to 7.30.1, which fixes two process-crash issues.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/v4.1.26...v4.1.27

name: SDK v0.2.1
body:
- `read_files` results are no longer re-cut to the 8k tool-result cap on the way to the provider. They use the 50k file-content cap, so a read the tool reported in full arrives in full. Command, search, MCP and custom tool results keep the 8k cap, and an explicit tool-result cap still applies
- Models that need interleaved reasoning get a placeholder `reasoning_content` on assistant messages that have none. This fixes Reflection Beam's `400 Missing required parameter: 'messages[n].reasoning_content'` after compaction or a model switch. The fact is carried as `ModelInfo.metadata.interleavedReasoningField`
- The summarizer now states a preference to go without reasoning instead of disabling it outright. The gateway disables it only for models whose catalog entry advertises an off option. Before, uncatalogued models got `reasoning_effort: "none"`, which some endpoints reject, and compaction fell back to basic
- A custom model with saved overrides now has `reasoning` seeded into its capability list unless it sets `supportsReasoning: false`, so an explicit reasoning disable reaches the provider. Before, gpt-5.6 and gpt-6 chat-completions endpoints rejected every tool call
- The native OpenAI adapter fits the reasoning level to the model's advertised effort ladder, so `max` and Extra High are no longer sent verbatim to GPT-5.x and o-series models that reject them
- LiteLLM: the legacy `max_tokens` is no longer used as the input budget when `max_output_tokens` is set. Null limits are treated as missing
- The `cline` provider's bundled default is now the first bundled free model. `resolveClineDefaultModelId()` in `@cline/core` returns the first free model from the live recommended feed, then the bundled one, then `CLINE_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID`
- `CLINE_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` is now `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, and the remaining hardcoded default-model literals use it. `@cline/shared` adds `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` for Anthropic's bare id format
- A running compaction can be stopped, and cancellations are counted in telemetry
- Session config and the hub RPC schema accept the `max` reasoning effort
- With tools and spawning enabled, core registers `ux_verifier`, which delegates an ordered checklist to a subagent through the host's `spawn_agent` executor. Disabling `spawn_agent` disables it too
- `createUxVerificationReportTool()` creates the opt-in `report_ux_verification` tool for structured reports with captions, pass/fail/blocked results and screenshot references
- `createPublishArtifactsTool({ publish })` creates the opt-in `publish_artifacts` tool. `createArtifactPublisher` from `@cline/core/cloud` publishes to cloud sessions through signed upload policies. Artifact IDs default to the source filename
- `McpToolDescriptor.annotations` carries a server's tool hints (`readOnlyHint` and friends) through the stdio and URL clients and the manager cache. `task.tool_used` telemetry gains `mode`
- `session.resume` starts a runtime for a saved session ID and reads history on the hub, instead of requiring `initialMessages`
- Cloud task creation accepts `initialMessage` to create and send in one call, and `localGit` to launch from a captured Git snapshot
- `HubCloudSessionClient.getArtifactDownloadUrl(sessionId, artifactId)` returns a signed URL without starting the sandbox
- Provider, model, MCP and MCP OAuth management are available as hub commands, with token authentication required for provider management
- The hub can return session history in bounded chunks and archived cloud history
- The hub validates caller accounts for cloud commands, and no longer re-sends a rejected Cline refresh token on every cloud poll
- Hub cloud requests no longer duplicate the API prefix
- Hub session handlers are retained when a session deletion fails
- Confirmed cloud handoff publication is exported from `@cline/core/cloud` for direct hosts
- `@cline/shared` adds `resolveClineAppUrl`, and the account response carries `dataPrivacyPath` for the web app's privacy settings page
- `@cline/ui` adds `SectionHeading`, `Banner`, `ItemCard`, `DetailList`, controlled `Dialog` components and a UX verification report carousel with screenshot downloads. Buttons, badges and switches are refreshed (loading and pending states, a small switch size), along with the colour tokens and a new `text-xxs` step
- Removed the `CLINE_CAPTURE_*` provider request capture, which wrote full request bodies to disk
- Every SDK package now includes its license file
- Refreshed the model catalog (6,457 → 7,621 models). Adds 94 providers from models.dev and drops Lilac and Tempr. The Cline recommended list adds Muse Ember. The Cline free list drops Reflection Beam, Laguna S 2.1 and Solar Mini 4, so the `cline` provider's bundled default is Nemotron 3.5 Super VL. ClinePass drops DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Mimo V2.6 Flash, Mimo V2.6 Pro, MiniMax M3, Qwen3.7 Plus and Qwen3.7 Max. Default models change for 67 other providers, mostly to Kimi K3.1 Pro, Gemini 4 Neon (including the `gemini` and `vertex` providers) or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. Qwen models now report tiered families such as `qwen-plus` and `qwen-max`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/sdk/sdk/v0.2.0...sdk/sdk/v0.2.1

name: 1.27.0 — LaTeX for formula regions from the text layer
body:
Changes since 1.26.1:

- Read formula regions as LaTeX from the PDF's own text layer: `extract_math_latex_in_regions_mem` (Node: `extractMathLatexInRegions`) rebuilds sub- and superscripts from glyph baselines and sizes, limits of `\sum`, `\int`, `\lim` and other large operators, accents, font alphabets (`\mathbb`, `\mathcal`, `\mathfrak`, `\mathbf`) and delimiters stacked from TeX extension-font pieces. Each region carries a gate saying whether its text layer was read: an invisible (OCR) layer, more than a tenth undecodable glyphs, or a region mostly outside math fonts on a page with next to no math fonts is reported and left empty. Fractions, radicals, matrices and multi-line displays are not rebuilt (#677).
- CI fetches ONNX Runtime 1.27.0 from the PyPI wheel, since the release asset is gone (#678).

API: new function only; existing extraction paths and the Node, Python and WebAssembly bindings are unchanged.

Release preparation: #680.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/firecrawl/pdf-inspector/compare/v1.26.1...v1.27.0)

name: v16.0.2
body:
## Critical fix

- **An auto-update no longer deletes the plugin version a running Claude Code session was loaded from** (#6352, thanks @0xABCD01, closes #6349 reported by @justindrp). The cache sweep keeps a version folder while the Claude Code process recorded in its `.in_use` file is alive. On macOS and BSD, a few seconds of difference between the start time Claude Code recorded and the one `ps` reports was read as PID reuse, so the sweep deleted the folder from under a live session and every hook failed for the rest of that session. A start-time mismatch no longer removes the folder while the process at that PID is still Claude Code. A PID that now belongs to another program is still pruned as before.
- **Every cache prune now logs why and who.** The worker writes one log line per removed version with its reason (orphaned or superseded) and the `.in_use` records it rejected and why (process exited or start-time mismatch), so any removal can be traced from the log alone.

## Fixes

- **The session-start card is drawn on Team and Enterprise accounts** (#6353, thanks @KeithMoc, closes #6314 reported by @TimoWestland). When an organization plugin runs first and the card's usual hooks never fire, the card now asks for itself from the `session.start` hook and the context hook answers it.
- **My Work detects OpenCode 2.x connections** (#6340, thanks @ZedingZhang, closes #6339 reported by @Realauster). The login probe reads OpenCode's JSON output, so a connected provider is no longer reported as logged out on OpenCode 2.3.2.
- **My Work refresh prefers MXC for isolated Codex launches on Windows** (#6348, thanks @QuantScorpus, refs #5163). The refresh no longer picks the unelevated sandbox and fails before the agent starts.
- **Both host-observer probes give a slow observer the same 1 s** (#6359, thanks @rtmalikian, closes #6358). The async probe used 400 ms and the install-time probe 1 s, so one called a valid observer "occupied" and the other did not.
- **Chroma collection deletes that lose their reply are checked before a rebuild** (#6338, thanks @POWDER-RANGER). The worker lists collections once instead of replaying the delete, and only rebuilds once the delete is confirmed.
- **chroma-mcp restarts after a cancelled read once in-flight writes settle** (#6337, thanks @MaxWang007). The next call no longer goes to a server that can no longer read its input.
- **Worker errors and unknown paths answer in JSON** (#6341, thanks @DeryFerd). The worker now installs its 404 and error handlers, so it no longer returns Express's HTML error page with local file paths in the stack trace.
- **CLAUDE.md placement resolves absolute paths before the project check** (#6336, thanks @LeviReisJs). Forward-slash paths on Windows are no longer dropped, and paths that climb out of the project with `..` are refused.
- **`npx claude-mem doctor` reads the worker's doctor endpoint once** (#6344, thanks @DeryFerd), so a slow worker costs one timeout instead of two.
- **The Agent Cost Report skill uses a spec-compliant name** (#6356, thanks @LuckVd, refs #6355), so agents that check skill names load it.

## New

- **Codex as an observer quota fallback** (#6326, thanks @QuantScorpus). When Claude hits its quota guard, the observer can use the local Codex CLI signed in with ChatGPT and return to Claude through the existing recovery path.
- **WorldRouter preset for the OpenAI-compatible provider** (#6357, thanks @Opgeek-1).
- **The startup card shows the Claude-Mem mark** in a right column when the terminal is wide enough (#6333).

## Tests, CI and docs

- A DNS-rebinding test pins the worker's Host guard ahead of CORS (#6345, thanks @DeryFerd).
- The Windows build runs the postinstall allowlist guard (#6343, thanks @DeryFerd).
- Devin cloud needs one org secret to connect CMEM Pro (#6335).
- The Docker pinning example says to build from the repository root (#6346, thanks @DeryFerd).

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v16.0.1...v16.0.2

name: graphify 0.9.114
body:
Performance work on the extract/build/update pipeline, plus a batch of extractor and build fixes. Every entry marked Perf preserves graph output exactly (byte-identical); the extractor fixes change output and share one AST cache schema bump (see the note at the end).

- Perf: **ids** `normalize_id` gets an ASCII fast-path, pre-compiled regexes and an LRU cache, so the common (ASCII, repeated) identifier case skips the Unicode normalization loop. ~1.26x on the compute path and a large win on repeated ids, which recurs heavily across a corpus.
- Perf: **cache** `save_cached` builds the portable on-disk payload copy-on-write instead of `copy.deepcopy`-ing every per-file result; ~20% faster on the cache-write transform, scaling with per-file graph size. The input is never mutated and the on-disk bytes are identical.
- Perf: **extract** each source file is read from disk once (the key hash and the parse share one buffer) instead of twice on a cold build, and the tree-sitter `Parser` is reused per language within a worker instead of rebuilt per file (file reads roughly halved on the worker path).
- Perf: **extract** the cross-file resolution finalize builds its shared node/edge indexes in a few fused passes instead of ~6 independent full scans of the graph; ~15% faster on the finalize stage.
- Perf: **watch** the no-change topology comparison uses an order-independent content hash computed in one pass instead of sorting and re-serializing the whole graph; ~1.4x on that compare.
- Perf: **cluster** the community partition is cached by a topology hash and reused when the graph is unchanged (~9x on a cluster cache hit), and the deterministic edge-sort key drops a per-edge `json.dumps` in favour of a cheap tuple key (identical ordering).
- Perf: **analyze** `suggest_questions`' betweenness centrality now runs a flat-array Brandes implementation instead of networkx's dict-based one, with bit-for-bit identical scores; ~2.6x faster, growing with graph size (#5303, thanks @Max17190).
- Perf: **watch** each preserved source path is rebased once per incremental update instead of recomputed per node and edge; the update output is byte-identical (#5322, thanks @Max17190).
- Fix: **java** a field or class annotated with Lombok `@Getter` gets the synthesized `getX()`/`isX()` getter node javac sees, so `obj.getX()` resolves to it; boolean fields use `isX`, `@Getter(AccessLevel.NONE)` is respected, a hand-written getter is not duplicated, and a non-Lombok `@Getter` is ignored (#5148, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **kotlin** a member call on a receiver with a declared type (parameter, property, `val x: T`, or `val x = T()`) binds to that type's method across files instead of the last same-named method in the file, and interface calls dispatch to their implementers; an ambiguous or unknown receiver fails closed (#5355, thanks @xiongjianxu).
- Fix: **sql** a PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL routine body that the grammar only parses through ERROR recovery (`RETURN QUERY SELECT ... FROM t`) has its table reads recovered as `reads_from` edges instead of dropped (#5349, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **build** when an AST-extracted edge and a semantic (LLM) copy of the same edge tie, the deterministic EXTRACTED edge is kept, so a later docs `--update` no longer deletes a code edge that a semantic copy had overwritten (#5334, thanks @Ildar-gn).
- Fix: **sql** a T-SQL procedure whose header the grammar only partly parses (tree-sitter-sql 0.3.12+ misreads the name, absorbing unparenthesised params or a `""`/`]]` escape) yields a single routine node instead of a duplicate under the misread id; a real routine sharing the misread's line is kept (#5236, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **vbnet** a method declared after a multi-line string literal is no longer dropped: the file is reparsed with multi-line strings flattened to a line-preserving placeholder first, so an unterminated string on one line no longer swallows the rest of the class; single-line files are parsed unchanged (#5320, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **cpp** a `std::`-qualified type (`std::chrono::seconds`, `std::vector<T>`) is no longer rewired onto a same-named project symbol; the std reference gets its own sourceless stub the corpus rewire skips, while the std type's template arguments still resolve to the project's own types (#5219, thanks @deba2k5).
- Fix: **python** a plain `import mod` where `mod` sits on a `sys.path.insert(...)` directory (a non-package script dir) now binds `mod.func()` to the `func` function node, matched to the unique file on that path and failing closed on ambiguity or a stdlib name; a `calls` edge is no longer aliased onto a file node (#5253, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
- Fix: **serve** a query that filters on the `call` relation now keeps cross-repo `calls` edges (written as `relation=calls, context=cross_repo`), which were silently dropped by the context-only filter (#5257, thanks @LHopitalOne).
- Fix: **build** a member's structural `method`/`contains` edge to its owner is kept over an opposite-direction member-usage edge (a method reading its class's own static property or constant), so the member no longer vanishes from the type's walk; non-usage relations (inherits/implements) keep the existing rule (#2391, thanks @livingforelvis).

The AST cache schema is bumped to 50; warm caches re-run the affected Kotlin, Java, SQL, VB.NET, C++ and Python (sys.path import) extractions.

- The judge asks as one more turn of the run, so the provider reads the run from its cache instead of billing the trace again. It returns the same verdict fields, gotchas included (#6457).

# Cua Driver 0.56.4

## Summary

## Fixes

- restore macOS web type_text keys and unhide reopened apps. ([#8434](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8434))

## Contributors

This release contains maintainer changes only.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

Windows:

```powershell
irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex
```

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds,
and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and
uninstaller scripts.

## Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest”
pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua
Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on
their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned
`cua-driver-rs-v*` releases directly.
